rationale: The child questions still carried plan-style discriminators from when they were registered, while the main question's was refreshed to what was observed. This update restates each child discriminator as the observation that actually carried it, with the receipt and indices, so a reader of the index sees how each answer was obtained rather than what was originally intended. No records other than the discriminators change.

investigations.discriminator: Observed discriminators: the identical pre-vote from the up-to-date candidate, delivered before and after the accepted message and again after the repair heartbeat. The before and after-restore deliveries produced no response while the post-forgery delivery produced a grant (indices 4, 6, 8 of CheckRun 4dd05e7a3c6b4894ad3c7d66fe58a201, with the window measured as one further leader tick producing the repair heartbeat at index 7), and the quorum stream showed the same forgery carrying the candidate through the pre-vote, the vote and leadership at term 3 (indices 13, 14, 15, 17).

Observed discriminator: the new leader's first append delivered to the deposed incumbent after the forged election. The incumbent accepted it (rejected=false), became StateFollower at term 3 following the new leader, and the append anchored at the committed prefix it already had, with its own uncommitted term-2 entry replaced (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a); a mismatch or entry loss would have widened the finding, and none appeared.

Observed discriminator: three consecutive rounds, each delivering the leader's real heartbeat, the same forged message and the same retried pre-vote, with each round's admissions kept separate. The control round granted nothing (index 29 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849) while every forged round granted (32, 35, 38) and the repair restored the context in the rounds that needed it (33, 36), so the repeated failure is the sender's cadence, not a broken repair.

Observed discriminator: three deliveries through the public Node.Step of a real RestartNode, read back through Node.Status. The genuinely local type left the reported leader at 1, the peer-form forged message cleared it to 0 without error, and Node.ForgetLeader produced the same 1 -> 0 transition (indices 41, 42, 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40).

Observed discriminator: a real election, then twenty leader ticks with nothing delivered in either direction. The leader was already StateFollower at its first election timeout with its term unchanged, and still a follower at the second sample (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512), so its own quorum check ended the leadership inside one election timeout.

Observed discriminator: queue a read request while the leader has no commit in its term, then complete the commit and the release round trip. No read state appeared for the request while the node was not yet able to answer it (index 48 of CheckRun d7a20d42d5b84569a0c6e4924cd577a9), and the released state then carried the commit index at release time with the original context (indices 49, 50).

Observed discriminator: demote the node that owes the request and later let it lead again. No read state appeared for the request while the node was a follower and its term was unchanged (index 52 of CheckRun 478561f525b3471ca92b9aa20c6d12df), and after it led again and committed, the stale request was released with the later index and its original context (index 54).
